desk.headline: Normalised EPS up 9.5% to 109.8c as margins widen on flat revenue of R25.5bn; dividend up 14.3% to 40c; FY2027 targets about 5% revenue growth
results: Revenue rose only 1.7% to R25.5bn, but cost control lifted normalised EBITDA 6.7% and widened the margin by 0.8 percentage points.

Normalised EPS, the company's preferred measure, rose 9.5% to 109.8c. Headline EPS of 98.4c compares with a loss of 112.1c a year ago, when a R2.9bn write-up of the Piramal liability tied to the Life Molecular Imaging sale hit earnings.
Patient days grew just 0.3% for the year (0.9% in the second half) and occupancy was 69.6%, below last year's aim of about 1% growth.
Net debt rose to 1.06 times EBITDA from almost zero after last year's special payout; a share buyback started in August, with 16.9 million shares bought at an average R11.75.
The final dividend rose 14.3% to 40c; impairments of R107m hit mainly non-acute businesses.

guidance.summary: For FY2027 Life targets about 5% revenue growth, about 1% patient-day growth and occupancy near 69%, with capex of about R1.9bn. It adds 158 acute beds, including the 140-bed Life Paarl Valley Hospital in Q4, and says it is on track for R400m of savings over three years.

points: CEO Peter Wharton-Hood called it a resilient year, with a much stronger second half, but said times are tough.
He blamed first-half weakness mainly on a medical scheme placed under curatorship and more doctors leaving.
In the second half the group focused on underperforming units and recruited 169 new doctors, whom he called the main drivers of hospital revenue.
Management stressed the R400m three-year savings plan and continued focus on the EBITDA margin.
call.source: EWN (26 Nov 2026) and Business Day (26 Nov 2026) coverage of the results

watch: Whether patient days pick up towards the 1% target after only 0.3% growth in FY2026.
Delivery of the R400m savings plan and the asset optimisation update due with the H1 FY2027 results.
The opening of Life Paarl Valley Hospital in Q4 FY2027 and approval for the two cyclotrons.
